sentences.text: Every morning the inventor carried water from a stone well to a row of herb pots.
The bucket had no cover, and water jumped over the rim with every step.
By the time the inventor reached the pots, a dark wet trail showed how much had been lost.
She marked the water line with chalk before one trip and again at the end.
The second mark was much lower. The problem could be measured, not merely grumbled about.
First she tried a wooden cover that sat loosely on top.
The cover slid off on the stairs and made the spill even worse.
Next she tied the cover down with string. The string held, but it was slow to untie at every pot.
The inventor watched her own hands and noticed that speed mattered as much as a tight cover.
She bent a small metal clasp that could snap shut and snap open with a press.
She tested the bucket ten times, chalk marks and all, and wrote each result in a notebook.
Less water was lost, and the cover came off quickly when she needed to pour.
One morning the clasp bent too far and would not catch. She shaped it again and tested once more.
The useful bucket was not one lucky thought.
It was a measured problem, a cover that failed, and a fastener that survived being tested.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: Finding a new well that never spills
Growing herbs without any water
Improving a bucket by measuring, trying, and testing
Throwing away notebooks after one idea

questions.explanation: The inventor measures the spill, tries a loose cover, tries string, then a clasp, and keeps testing. Improvement through tests is the main idea.

questions.prompt: What fails on the first try?

choices.text: The stone well runs dry
The chalk will not write
The metal clasp snaps open too easily
A loose wooden cover slides off

questions.explanation: The first fix is a wooden cover that sits loosely and slides off on the stairs. The clasp comes later and works better.

questions.prompt: From the story, a clasp is what?

choices.text: A fastener that can snap shut and snap open
A chalk line on a bucket
A trail of spilled water
A notebook full of herbs

questions.explanation: The inventor bends a small metal clasp that can snap shut and snap open. Those actions show that a clasp is a fastener.

questions.prompt: Why does she mark the water line with chalk?

choices.text: So the herbs can read the bucket
So she can see how much water is lost, not just feel annoyed
So the string will stick to the wood
So the well will refill by itself

questions.explanation: The story says the second mark was lower and that the problem could be measured. The chalk is a way to compare the start and the end of a trip.

questions.prompt: What is the order of the tries?

choices.text: Clasp, then string, then a loose cover
String, then chalk, then no test at all
Loose cover, then string, then a metal clasp
Notebook, then well, then a broken stair

questions.explanation: She tries the loose wooden cover first, then string, and then the clasp that snaps. The tests continue after that order.
